local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 every New Jersey county elects members of its Board of County Commissioners, and some counties also elect a county clerk, sheriff, surrogate or county executive, all by party. Most municipalities elect a mayor, council members or township committee members by party the same day; some municipalities hold nonpartisan elections in May instead (a few have moved theirs to November, where they appear without party). Most school boards are elected on November 3 without party, and some fire districts have moved their elections to November too. Districts that kept an April school election, fire districts that vote in February, special school elections and any December runoffs are other days. The Governor and the Legislature are elected in odd years, and judges are appointed.
local_calendar.s: The Division of Elections' 2026 General Election chronological timeline and the county clerks' lists for November 3, 2026

local_coverage.t: Loaded: every contest between people on the county clerks' lists for 7 of the 21 counties (Bergen, Gloucester, Middlesex, Morris, Ocean, Passaic, Union): 15 county contests, 307 municipal contests, 279 school board contests and 4 fire district contests, with 1589 names. Left out: the 14 counties whose lists are not loaded yet (each is listed with the reason); ballot questions; the federal contests on the county lists, which come from the state's own certification; and a party's line that reads no nomination was made. Bergen's and Passaic's lists for county and municipal offices are marked unofficial by their clerks; the county's sample ballot is the authority.
